examples.instruction: Start from each `train` record; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the number of records in the group.

examples.sql: SELECT "train"."Railway_ID" AS e, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "train" GROUP BY "train"."Railway_ID" ORDER BY m1 DESC LIMIT 10
examples.instruction: Start from each `train` record; group the kept records by Railway ID (`train.Railway_ID`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) Railway ID (`train.Railway_ID`); (2) the number of records in the group; order the result rows by the number of records in the group descending (missing last); keep only the first 10 rows.

examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "train"."Railway_ID" AS e, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "train" GROUP BY "train"."Railway_ID") SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS m1 FROM "s1"

examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "train"."Railway_ID" AS e, COUNT(*) AS m1 FROM "train" GROUP BY "train"."Railway_ID"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS v FROM "s1") SELECT "s1"."e" AS e, "s1"."m1" AS m1, (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS m2 FROM "s1" JOIN "s2" ON "s2"."v" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY m2 DESC LIMIT 10
